title: TTC: Digital Wayfinding & Information Architecture
subtitle: Restructured the TTC website's information architecture to prioritize rider tasks, reducing navigation confusion and improving task completion.
methods: IA audit, WCAG/AODA review, moderated usability testing, annotated wireframes
description: An information architecture audit and WCAG/AODA accessibility review of the Toronto Transit Commission's website, validated through moderated usability tests and translated into prioritized navigation, contrast, and content-structure improvements.
bullets: Conducted an information architecture audit and WCAG/AODA accessibility review to identify navigation and readability barriers.
Ran moderated usability tests to validate pain points across key journeys and quantify impact.
Proposed prioritized improvements to button hierarchy, color contrast, and content structure, and produced annotated wireframes and remediation recommendations for accessibility compliance.
challenge: Public transit riders often need information quickly — Is my train delayed? Which route should I take? How much will the trip cost? The TTC website is designed to answer these questions but finding those answers isn't always easy.
solution: Through usability evaluation and research-driven design improvements, restructured the IA to prioritize primary rider tasks over internal logic.
impact: Significantly reduced task completion time for common user journeys including trip planning and service alert lookup. Validated through usability testing with TTC riders.

sections.body: Public transit riders need information quickly: Is my train delayed? Which route should I take? How much will the trip cost? title: Kijiji — Trust & Safety System
subtitle: Designed a layered trust framework to reduce fraud and increase buyer confidence in peer-to-peer marketplace transactions.
methods: User research, journey mapping, system design, prototyping

challenge: Kijiji users frequently encounter scams, fraudulent listings, and safety concerns. Users hesitate when profiles are anonymous and listing quality is inconsistent.

title: BeaverBuild — Financial Literacy for Newcomers
subtitle: Designed a paced learning platform helping newcomer Ontario college students navigate Canadian finances — from Day 1 to Month 6.
users: Newcomer Ontario college students (international, low-income, recent immigrants)
methods: Interviews, UX audit, gap analysis, affinity mapping, ideation, high-fi prototyping, moderated usability testing
description: A team UX research and product-design project for a web platform helping newcomer Ontario college students understand and navigate Canadian finances through a paced, milestone-based learning experience.
challenge: Newcomer college students arrive in Ontario facing an immediate, high-stakes crash course in a financial system they've never touched. The information exists — but none of it was built for them.
solution: Pivoted from a content aggregator to a paced, milestone-based learning journey: Day 1 → Week 1 → Month 1 → Month 6.
impact: 5-person team. 4 newcomer interviews across 3 Ontario colleges. 5-participant usability test produced prioritized improvements across 5 themes.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.summary: The information exists. Acting on it doesn't.
sections.body: Newcomer students arriving at Ontario colleges face an immediate, high-stakes crash course in a financial system they have never touched. They are not failing because the information isn't out there — government sites, college workshops, and fintech apps are everywhere. They are failing because none of those resources were built for them.
bullets: Resources scattered across government portals, college emails, and bank websites
All assume baseline understanding of Canadian credit, taxes, and banking
Students spend first 6-12 months on debit only out of fear
No product treats newcomer students as a primary audience

sections.title: Key Insights
sections.summary: Three patterns, heard from every participant
bullets: Delayed financial confidence — Students limited themselves to debit for 6-12 months from fear of the unknown
Information overload & low visibility — College emails went unread, government sites felt cluttered
Reactive, not proactive — Students managed money by checking balances after the fact, not planning ahead

sections.title: The Pivot Moment
sections.summary: We almost built the wrong thing
sections.body: Early ideation pulled us toward a resource aggregator — essentially a better-organized Canada.ca. But the interviews surfaced something deeper: students lacked a mental model for Canadian finance. They didn't need more content organized more cleanly; they needed someone to tell them what matters on Day 1.
sections.body2: We shifted from a content hub to a paced milestone journey: a guide, not a library.

sections.title: Design Decisions
sections.summary: Every decision traced back to a research finding
bullets: Milestone-based timeline (Day 1 → Month 6) — temporal anchoring reduces cognitive load
Newcomer-first language — no jargon without plain-language explanation
Mobile-first, single-task screens — college portals were described as "cluttered"
Proactive push at enrollment — reach students before avoidance habits set in
Progress-visible design — "Month 1 of 6" rather than endless scroll

title: HabitPup — Gamified Habit Tracker with Virtual Pet System
subtitle: Designed and built a cross-platform habit tracker where completing habits keeps virtual pets alive — leveraging loss aversion and collection mechanics to solve the habit-tracker retention cliff.
users: Habit builders who've abandoned traditional trackers
methods: Retention research, gamification system design, full-stack development (React, React Native, Express, PostgreSQL)
description: A cross-platform habit tracker with a virtual pet gamification layer — users complete habits to earn currency, adopt pets, and keep them alive. Ships on web, iOS, Android, and as a Chrome extension.
bullets: Designed a virtual pet decay system leveraging loss aversion — pets lose hunger/thirst daily, and prolonged neglect causes level drops, creating genuine urgency to maintain habits.
Built a full-stack monorepo (pnpm workspaces) with OpenAPI-first contract design — a single spec generates both React Query hooks and Zod validation schemas.
Shipped across 4 surfaces: React web app, React Native mobile app (Expo SDK 54), Express 5 API, and Chrome MV3 browser extension.
challenge: Habit tracking apps have a well-documented retention cliff. Users download them with good intentions, log habits for a few days, then abandon them. The core issue: the reward loop is too abstract. Checking a box provides a brief dopamine hit, but there's no tangible, ongoing consequence to quitting.
solution: Introduced a virtual pet system where pets actively decay over time — hunger and thirst meters drop daily, and prolonged neglect causes visible level drops. Completing habits earns coins, food, and water to care for pets. Loss aversion replaces abstract motivation.
impact: Designed and developed the complete product across 4 platforms with 14 database tables, 24 virtual pet species, a multi-tier economy system, social features, and health metric tracking.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.summary: Habit trackers fail because quitting has no visible cost
sections.body: Habit tracking apps have a well-documented retention cliff. Users download them with good intentions, log habits for a few days, then abandon them. The core issue: the reward loop is too abstract. Checking a box provides a brief dopamine hit, but there's no tangible, ongoing consequence to quitting. The habit tracker becomes another forgotten app.
bullets: Checkbox-based trackers provide no emotional stakes
Streak counters motivate through pressure, not pleasure — and breaking a streak often causes total abandonment
No existing tracker makes the cost of quitting visible and personal

sections.title: My Role & Process
sections.summary: Solo product designer and full-stack developer — concept through deployment
bullets: Role: Product Designer & Full-Stack Developer (solo project)
Research: retention psychology, gamification mechanics, streak computation models
Design: system architecture, interaction design, neo-brutalist visual language
Development: React web, React Native mobile, Express API, PostgreSQL, Chrome extension

sections.title: Research & Design Foundation
sections.summary: Retention psychology pointed to two proven mechanics
sections.body: Before writing any code, I researched retention psychology, gamification frameworks, and existing habit tracker UX patterns. Two insights shaped the design direction:
bullets: Loss aversion — people work harder to avoid losing something they already have than to gain something new (Kahneman & Tversky)
Collection completion drives — incomplete sets create psychological tension that motivates action (Zeigarnik effect applied to collecting)
Streak mechanics alone create anxiety after breaks — the Duolingo research confirmed this pattern
sections.body2: The design question became: what if your habits kept something alive?

sections.title: Key Insights
sections.summary: Three patterns that shaped the product
bullets: Tangible stakes beat abstract metrics — a starving pet is more motivating than a broken streak
Decay creates genuine urgency — unlike a checkbox that waits for you, a pet actively deteriorates without attention
Collection pressure drives re-engagement — seeing pets you don't have creates soft motivation to keep earning

sections.title: System Design
sections.summary: A multi-layered economy connecting habits to pet wellbeing
sections.body: The core loop connects habit completion to pet care through a virtual economy. Completing habits awards coins, food, and water. Coins buy pets (24 species, 50–320 coins), toys, and training sessions. Food and water restore hunger and thirst meters. But the meters decay daily — creating a continuous need to maintain habits.
bullets: Pet decay: hunger/thirst drop 10 points/day. Level down if either hits 0 for 24+ hours. Level up if both stay above 70% for 24+ hours.
Care activities: Walk (4hr decay reset, 1hr cooldown), Bath (2-day reset, 12hr cooldown), Play (3hr reset, 30min cooldown)
Food tiers: Kibble (restores 20), Treat (restores 35), Premium (restores 50 + instant level-up)
Training: costs 5 coins, 30min cooldown. Every 5 tricks learned grants a level-up.
Visitor system: random unowned pets appear every 6 hours — playing with them awards 15 coins and refreshes all pet play meters

sections.title: Architecture Decisions
sections.summary: OpenAPI-first monorepo with generated clients
sections.body: The most impactful architectural decision was making the OpenAPI 3.1 specification the single source of truth for the entire API contract. From this one YAML file, Orval generates TanStack Query hooks for the clients and Zod validation schemas for the server. If the API changes, both clients and server validation update in a single codegen run.
bullets: pnpm workspace monorepo with 4 shippable artifacts and 5 shared libraries
OpenAPI-first: one spec → generated React Query hooks + Zod schemas (no contract drift)
Clerk authentication across all surfaces with custom userScope middleware for per-user data isolation
Three-tier rate limiting: general (100/min), write (30/min), financial (10/min)
Timezone-aware date handling — 'today' computed in user's local time via X-Habit-Calendar-Timezone header

sections.title: Visual Design
sections.summary: Neo-brutalist aesthetic that stands apart in a sea of minimalist trackers
sections.body: The web frontend uses a distinctive brutalist aesthetic — thick borders, hard drop shadows, bold oversized typography, and high-contrast color palette. This isn't just aesthetic preference: the thick, high-contrast UI elements are easy to tap on mobile web, and the bold visual language makes the app instantly recognizable.
bullets: Thick borders and hard shadows create depth without skeuomorphism
Bold typography scales well across screen sizes
High contrast meets accessibility requirements for outdoor mobile use
Radix UI primitives provide accessible interaction patterns underneath the visual layer

sections.title: Streak Computation
sections.summary: Handling daily and scheduled habits differently
sections.body: Not all habits are daily. Some run on specific weekdays (e.g., gym on Mon/Wed/Fri). The streak algorithm handles both cases: for daily habits, it walks backward over every day. For scheduled habits, it walks backward over only target days. The dashboard endpoint batch-fetches completions for the last 400 days and computes all streaks in-memory, avoiding N+1 queries.
bullets: Daily habits: every consecutive day counts toward the streak
Scheduled habits: only target weekdays count (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri)
Batch computation: all streaks calculated in a single pass over 400 days of data
Timezone-safe: all date operations use the user's local timezone, not UTC

sections.title: Cross-Platform Delivery
sections.summary: Four surfaces, one API, shared type contracts
sections.body: The product ships on four surfaces, all consuming the same API through generated type-safe hooks:
bullets: Web: React 19 + Vite 7 + Tailwind v4 + TanStack Query v5
Mobile: React Native 0.81 + Expo SDK 54 + Expo Router + push notifications
API: Express 5 + Drizzle ORM + PostgreSQL (Neon) + Pino logging
Extension: Chrome MV3 + vanilla JS + chrome.storage.local
sections.body2: Mobile-specific features include Android Health Connect integration for automatic step/sleep data sync, AdMob rewarded ads, and EAS cloud builds for App Store/Play Store submission.

sections.title: Social & Health Features
sections.summary: Beyond habits — community and wellness tracking
sections.body: The product extends beyond habit tracking into social accountability and health monitoring:
bullets: Friend system: unique friend codes, send/accept/decline requests, undirected edge storage (userA < userB)
Leaderboards: ranked by coins or total completions, scoped to friends-only or global
Health metrics: steps, calories, sleep, standups, heart rate with configurable goals and 7-day history
Grocery list: per-user shopping list with check/uncheck, reorder, and bulk-clear

sections.title: Security & Reliability
sections.summary: Supply-chain defense and multi-tier rate limiting
sections.body: Security was considered from the start, not bolted on later:
bullets: Supply-chain defense: pnpm enforces 1-day minimum release age for npm packages, preventing compromised package consumption
Per-user data isolation: every query scoped to Clerk userId via userScope middleware — no cross-user data access possible
Three-tier rate limiting: general (100 req/min), write operations (30 req/min), financial operations (10 req/min)
Structured logging: Pino for production-grade request/error logging

sections.title: Impact & Results
sections.summary: Full product designed and shipped across 4 platforms
bullets: Designed and built the complete product end-to-end: 14 database tables, 24 pet species, multi-tier economy, social system, health tracking
Shipped on 4 surfaces (web, iOS, Android, Chrome extension) from a single monorepo
OpenAPI-first architecture eliminated frontend/backend contract drift entirely
560-line deployment guide makes the project fully independent of any single platform
sections.body2: The pet decay system is the core differentiator — unlike streak counters that create anxiety, caring for a virtual pet reframes habit maintenance as nurturing rather than performance.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.summary: Gamification works when quitting has visible, emotional cost
sections.body: This project reinforced that the most effective retention mechanics aren't about rewards — they're about consequences. A checkbox is forgettable. A starving virtual pet is not. Loss aversion is a powerful lever, but it has to be balanced: too much pressure causes abandonment, too little causes indifference. The decay rate (10 points/day) and recovery mechanics (food tiers, care activities) were designed to create urgency without anxiety.
